sources: Live GitHub/API/npm research 2026-11-14 (three parallel research operations; every field verified from primary sources: repo metadata, LICENSE files, READMEs, npm/PyPI registries, official docs)

records.name: OpenViking
records.provenance: volcengine (ByteDance cloud brand); 42,221 stars; pushed 2026-11-14; VLDB 2026 / ICDE papers (VikingMem, TrieHI, VikingRAG)
records.decisionRationale: Capability match is excellent (all memory requirements) and stewardship is strong. AGPL-3.0 is fine for internal use but source obligations apply if modified and offered as a network service; the heavyweight Rust+Python+React server is disproportionate for the current single-service CPU deployment. Adopted as the reference architecture and adapter target behind the MemoryBackend seam; native SQLite engine remains the default backend.
compatibility: Node/Bun clients via REST gateway (when self-hosted)
records.securityAssessment: ACL model + per-directory permissions verified in docs; AGPL licence review required before hosted deployment

testResults.name: capability-vs-requirements matrix
testResults.detail: 9/9 memory requirements matched from verified docs

records.upgradeStrategy: Pin v0.5.x; re-evaluate self-hosting when memory workloads exceed native engine capacity

records.name: Pizza Bot
records.provenance: 559 stars; pushed 2026-11-13; DeepAgents/LangGraph runtime; Electron+Hono monorepo
records.decisionRationale: Proven orchestration patterns (durable queues, checkpoint/resume, HITL approval durability) extracted into NAEI's own multi-tenant orchestrator. Not adopted wholesale: it is a single-user personal inbox, not a workforce fabric; no multi-tenancy, no peer delegation, no fleet semantics.
records.integrationAdapter: packages/naei (patterns: durable task queue, checkpointing, approval gates)
records.securityAssessment: Apache-2.0, no copyleft concerns; its unauthenticated local sockets are a known weakness we do not replicate

testResults.name: pattern fit analysis
testResults.detail: 7/10 NAEI requirements matched; gaps documented (multi-tenant, peer delegation, SLA layer)

records.upgradeStrategy: Track releases; re-evaluate its standalone backend if NAEI needs a desktop inbox UX

records.name: ARTEMIS (Google)
records.provenance: Google; 17,426 stars; iOS support open PR #175 (2026-10-07, unmerged; requires macOS + Xcode 27 host)
records.decisionRationale: Matches every stated requirement for Android device automation and testing with real evidence collection; Apache-2.0; daemon runs on Linux. iOS cannot be satisfied by ARTEMIS today (Android-only; open iOS PR requires macOS+Xcode host) — the iOS path adapts Appium XCUITest + WebDriverAgent (+ go-ios) per research.
records.integrationAdapter: Planned: MCP registration (stdio/HTTP) once a device host exists
records.securityAssessment: Requires an LLM API key per run; on-device accessibility helper; evidence streams stored locally
records.blockedBy: No Android device/emulator host in the build environment
records.upgradeStrategy: Watch PR #175 (native iOS); until merged, pair with Appium/WDA for iPhone-from-Linux

records.name: Unsloth
records.decisionRationale: Best-in-class QLoRA efficiency with Apache-2.0 core and export targets matching an OpenAI-compatible serving plan. Training requires NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPU or Apple Silicon (QLoRA 7-8B needs >= 5-6GB VRAM) — CPU-only supports chat + data prep, NOT training. Adoption therefore targets off-platform training (free Colab/Kaggle T4) with Railway limited to orchestration + serving via API providers.
records.integrationAdapter: Planned: model-lab workflows (dataset prep CPU-able; training on Colab/Kaggle; GGUF export tracked in registry)
records.securityAssessment: Core Apache-2.0; avoid AGPL Studio components in hosted services
records.blockedBy: No GPU in build environment or Railway deployment
records.upgradeStrategy: Monthly releases; pin in Colab notebook requirements

records.name: Godot Engine
records.provenance: Verified from LICENSE.txt + official docs; releases 2026-08-22
capabilities: --headless server mode on Linux (no GPU/display required)
records.decisionRationale: Genuine advantage for headless CI testing of game logic and lightweight utilities/prototyping. Explicitly NOT a second world runtime — Unreal remains primary (engine-level constraint documented).
records.integrationAdapter: Planned: headless test harness in CI for simulation logic ports

records.name: Unity
records.licence: Proprietary (Personal free < $200k revenue; runtime fee cancelled Sept 2024, verified)
records.decisionRationale: No measurable advantage over Unreal+Blender for this project; would introduce a second heavy runtime competing with UE5; seat-metered licensing above $200k; governance risk history (2023 runtime fee episode, 2026 price increases). MCP lead closed by Epic's native Unreal MCP. CoplayDev/unity-mcp retained as design reference only.

records.name: MCP TypeScript SDK
records.decisionRationale: Official SDK; powers the NEXUS MCP gateway and bundled test server; MIT.
compatibility: Bun runtime verified by live integration tests
records.securityAssessment: Standard; credentials isolated per server registration

records.name: MCP Registry (modelcontextprotocol.io)
records.decisionRationale: Gateway registration schema follows the server.json manifest format (name/title/description/version/transport) for day-one registry compatibility.

testResults.name: manifest-shaped registration
testResults.detail: registration schema validated in integration tests

records.name: FreeMoCap
capabilities: markerless motion capture from multi-camera video
records.decisionRationale: High relevance for NEXUS WORLD animation pipelines (video-to-animation feeding Blender). Deferred adoption: AGPL obligations + alpha status; adopt when animation production starts.

records.name: Natron
records.decisionRationale: Low priority: Blender compositor + UE Sequencer cover the pipeline; slow release cadence and maintainer scarcity are risks. Revisit only for long-cinematic render farms.

records.name: Theatre.js
records.provenance: 12,996 stars; last public activity 2024-08-14; 1.0 in private repo
records.decisionRationale: Marginal: UE5 owns cinematic animation; no web runtime in NEXUS WORLD; stalled public development. Revisit only if a Three.js dashboard needs choreography.

records.name: Unreal Engine native MCP
records.provenance: Official Epic documentation (live fetch); Streamable HTTP inside editor; community: ChiR24/Unreal_mcp 'EngineWire' 1,036 stars (450+ capabilities, pushed 2026-11-13); kevinpbuckley/VibeUE 834 stars (native MCP expansion)
records.decisionRationale: First-party MCP surface materially strengthens 'Unreal stays primary' architecture. Registration manifests prepared; live connection requires the owner's UE 5.8+ editor host.
records.integrationAdapter: packages/mcp-gateway (HTTP transport registration, endpoint via env)
compatibility: UE 5.8+ editor running on owner workstation
records.securityAssessment: Local HTTP in-editor; token auth on EngineWire variant
records.blockedBy: Unreal Editor runs on the owner's workstation, not in this build environment

records.name: Blender MCP (mcp-for-blender)
records.provenance: 34,362 stars; PyPI mcp-for-blender 2026-11-13; stdio bridge + in-Blender socket (localhost:9876, NO auth — known weakness)
records.decisionRationale: De-facto standard Blender MCP; MIT; maps directly onto the gateway's stdio transport. Its unauthenticated socket is a documented security weakness the gateway mitigates via permission + approval layers.
records.securityAssessment: Unauthenticated localhost socket upstream; gateway enforces approval_required + allowlist; SAFE_MODE env supported
records.blockedBy: No Blender binary in build environment
